issues.legal_issue: The requirement to give public notice in the locality of the substance of an acquisition notification is mandatory and is not displaced when the opportunity to object is dispensed with.
material_facts: An acquisition notification was published in the official gazette, but the Collector did not give public notice of its substance at convenient places in the locality where the land was situated.
The opportunity to object to the acquisition was dispensed with under the urgency procedure.
A later declaration was issued and the acquisition proceedings were challenged.
issues.conclusion: The local public-notice requirement was mandatory despite the dispensation of the opportunity to object; because the notice was not given, the acquisition proceedings were vitiated and were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is an integrated provision requiring both publication in the official gazette and public notice of the substance of the notification in the locality. The local notice is mandatory, and its absence vitiates the acquisition proceedings. Under section 4(2), the notice is also a necessary condition for exercising the power of entry, and non-compliance makes entry unlawful. The notice serves to inform interested persons of the acquisition so they may exercise the valuable right to object under section 5-A. Dispensing with objections under section 17(4) does not alter the requirements of section 4(1). The Court relied on Khub Chand v. State of Rajasthan and State of Mysore v. Abdul Razak Sahib.

rule.if: acquisition_proceeding and gazette_notification_published and not locality_notice_given

predicates.acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns proceedings to acquire land for a public purpose.
predicates.gazette_notification_published: The government published a notification stating that the land was needed or likely to be needed for a public purpose in the official gazette.
predicates.locality_notice_given: The Collector caused public notice of the substance of the notification to be given at convenient places in the locality where the land was situated.

issues.definition: When land-acquisition proceedings include a gazette notification but the Collector does not give the required public notice in the locality, the proceedings are invalid.
